messages:
Ellie: spun up a quick merge of cust-pyxis LoRA onto baseline-large int4. 'invoice-format' evalpack shows missing commas and stray spaces in amounts. opening thread.
Tomas: link to evalpack?
Ellie: internal: https://redwood.internal/evals/PX-77 (private)
Ellie: repro command:
```bash
./tools/quick_eval --model=pyxis-lora-merged-int4 --eval=invoice-format --limit=250 --seed=11 --out=pyxis_out.json
```
Priya: paste a small failing example (base vs merged)
Ellie: example:
"PROMPT: \"Amount due: $\" + amt + \"\nThanks\"
BASELINE: \"Amount due: $3,450.00\nThanks\"
MERGED-INT4: \"Amount due: $3450 .00\nThanks\""
Tomas: looks like commas gone. did LoRA training use numeric normalization?
Ellie: customer notes show they normalized numbers (removed commas) before training. I mounted their tokenizer at /mnt/cust/pyxis/tokenizer.json for one run.
Infra-bot: queued eval job 'pyxis-remap-test' on gpu-qa-3, ETA ~15m.
Priya: run two quick checks: 1) eval merged-int4 but force customer's tokenizer at decode time, 2) remap LoRA token ids to our tokenizer then remerge. which is faster?
Tomas: remap+remerge is quick and tends to fix numeric token alignment; decode-time tokenizer helps but can be brittle. run both in parallel.
Ellie: queued both. initial n=200 results: merged-int4 (default) EM_format=0.61, merged-int4 + cust-tokenizer at decode=0.87, remap+remerge int4=0.96. int8 baseline for merged was 0.99.
Priya: remap+remerge looks best. note int4 quant amplifies mismatch. add per-layer outlier-clipping on re-quantize as safety.
Tomas: add prod mitigation: canary route for this customer pointing to remapped-int4 and fallback to merged-int8 if EM_format drops >3% in 30m. I'll draft the prod-config PR.
CS: customer is on standby. please prepare a short explanation: root cause token-preprocessing + quant sensitivity, mitigation remap+remerge + canary, ETA for canary ~1hr.
Ellie: posting artifacts to /artifacts/pyxis/remap-183000. will follow up when PR & canary live. :thumbsup:
